title: Two Views of the U.S. Embassy in Jerusalem

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 DealBook

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的舞台上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些举足轻重的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费畅享我们所有的深度报道一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: For Israelis, it's a historic milestone for the Jewish state.
sentences.zh: 对于以色列人来说，这是犹太国的一个历史性里程碑。

sentences.en: For Gazans, it's the latest betrayal of the Palestinian people.
sentences.zh: 对于加沙人来说，这是对巴勒斯坦人民的又一次背叛。

sentences.en: Two views of the relocation of the American embassy to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 美国大使馆搬迁至耶路撒冷带来的两种截然不同的视角。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月15日，星期二。

sentences.en: On behalf of the 45th president of the United States on America, we welcome you officially and for the first time to the embassy of the United States here in Jerusalem, the capital
sentences.zh: 谨代表美利坚合众国第45任总统，我们正式且首次欢迎各位来到美国驻耶路撒冷大使馆，这里是

sentences.en: of Israel.
sentences.zh: 以色列的首都。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: David, what's happening in Jerusalem on Monday?
sentences.zh: 大卫，周一耶路撒冷发生了什么？

sentences.en: So today, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner arrived here with the Treasury Secretary, with a delegation
sentences.zh: 今天，伊万卡·特朗普和贾里德·库什纳与财政部长一同抵达这里，随行的还有一个由美国国会参众两院议员组成的代表团，

sentences.en: of American members of Congress and the Senate, with a number of spiritual leaders from Jewish
sentences.zh: 以及美国犹太人

sentences.en: community and evangelical community in the United States, for a big ceremony marking the move of the United States embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 和福音派社区的多位精神领袖，共同出席庆祝美国大使馆从特拉维夫迁往耶路撒冷的盛大仪式。

sentences.en: David Halfinger is the Jerusalem bureau chief for the Times.
sentences.zh: 大卫·哈尔芬格是《时报》耶路撒冷分社社长。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, we are about to begin our ceremony.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，我们的仪式即将开始。

sentences.en: Please remember to silence your phones now.
sentences.zh: 请记得现在将手机静音。

sentences.en: Going back to the formation of the state of Israel, Jerusalem was going to be set aside in a way unto itself as a basically an international city.
sentences.zh: 回顾以色列国的成立，耶路撒冷原本打算作为一个独立的国际城市被特殊对待。

sentences.en: It wasn't given to either side.
sentences.zh: 它没有划给任何一方。

sentences.en: And for
sentences.zh: 对于

sentences.en: Israel today, which, you know, increasingly wants to be known as the nation state of the Jewish
sentences.zh: 今天的以色列来说，你知道的，它越来越希望被称为犹太人

sentences.en: people, for the United States to declare Jerusalem the capital of Israel and to move its embassy democracy here.
sentences.zh: 的民族国家，美国在这里宣布耶路撒冷为以色列首都并将民主大使馆搬迁至此。

sentences.en: To Jews, it's a vindication.
sentences.zh: 对犹太人来说，这是一次昭雪。

sentences.en: It's an acknowledgement of what they feel has been denied for some time now.
sentences.zh: 这是对他们认为长期以来被剥夺之物的承认。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please join me now in welcoming Ambassador David Friedman.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，请和我一起欢迎戴维·弗里德曼大使。

sentences.en: And please be seated.
sentences.zh: 请入座。

sentences.en: It began with the ambassador of the United States, David Friedman.
sentences.zh: 仪式由美国驻以大使戴维·弗里德曼拉开序幕。

sentences.en: He is a former bankruptcy lawyer for
sentences.zh: 他曾是特朗普总统

sentences.en: President Trump.
sentences.zh: 的破产案律师。

sentences.en: He's an Orthodox Jew.
sentences.zh: 他是一名正统犹太教徒。

sentences.en: On this exact day, 70 years ago, at almost this exact time, David Ben-Gurion declared Israel's independence.
sentences.zh: 就在整整70年前的今天，几乎在此时此刻，戴维·本-古里安宣布以色列独立。

sentences.en: Just 11 minutes later, President Harry Truman caused the United States to be the very first nation to recognize the reborn state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 仅仅11分钟后，哈里·杜鲁门总统使美国成为第一个承认新生的以色列国的国家。

sentences.en: Palestinians remember that time with a very different set of emotions.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦人对那段时期的记忆伴随着完全不同的一套情感。

sentences.en: May 15th for Palestinians is called Nakba Day.
sentences.zh: 对巴勒斯坦人而言，5月15日被称为“灾难日”。

sentences.en: It's the day they consider the catastrophe when hundreds of thousands of them were expelled from or fled from their homes in what became Israel.
sentences.zh: 在这一天，他们经历了灾难，成千上万的人在后来成为以色列的土地上被驱逐或逃离家园。

sentences.en: And for them, it's the day really of mourning.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这确实是一个哀悼日。

sentences.en: And so the idea that the United States was going to be making this move on the eve of that particular anniversary was seen by many as quite a provocation.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国竟然在这个特定纪念日前夕采取这一举动，在许多人看来是一种相当大的挑衅。

sentences.en: 70 years since that memorable event, almost to the minute, the United States finally takes the next step.
sentences.zh: 自那个难忘的事件过去70年，几乎分秒不差，美国终于迈出了下一步。

sentences.en: A step awaited, voted upon, litigated, and prayed for, for all these years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多年来备受期盼、投票表决、法律诉讼和祈祷的步骤。

sentences.en: Today, we open the United States Embassy in Jerusalem, Israel.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开设了美国驻以色列耶路撒冷大使馆。

sentences.en: So Mr. Friedman a number of times said he was welcoming them to the embassy in Jerusalem, Israel.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗里德曼先生多次表示，他欢迎他们来到以色列耶路撒冷的大使馆。

sentences.en: For many years, American children born in Israel, when they got their passports, those passports would say Jerusalem as the city, and the country would be left blank.
sentences.zh: 多年来，在以色列出生的美国儿童在获得护照时，护照上的城市会写耶路撒冷，而国家一栏则会留空。

sentences.en: Mr. Friedman was making a note in his own subtle way there that this is no more, that for the United States, Jerusalem is very much
sentences.zh: 弗里德曼先生在那里以他自己微妙的方式指出，这一切已经不复存在，对美国而言，耶路撒冷不仅仅是

sentences.en: a part, and not just a part, but the heart of the state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 以色列国的一部分，而且是核心。

sentences.en: So right from the beginning, we have this far-right representative of the United States president provocatively claiming that Jerusalem is the capital of Israel.
sentences.zh: 因此，从一开始，我们就看到美国总统这位极右翼代表挑衅性地宣称耶路撒冷是以色列的首都。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, the Palestinians have always felt that the United States was not exactly a neutral, unbiased arbiter of the peace process.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，巴勒斯坦人一直觉得美国并非和平进程中一个绝对中立、毫无偏见的仲裁者。

sentences.en: They've always had complaints that, you know, Israel was his ally, and the Palestinians always had to compete with that.
sentences.zh: 他们一直抱怨以色列是美国的盟友，而巴勒斯坦人总是不得不与这种关系竞争。

sentences.en: But now they're basically saying, look, I mean, all pretense has been dispensed with.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们基本上是在说，看吧，所有的伪装都已经撕破了。

sentences.en: The United States and Israel are solidly, like, just about in the same shoes, not just, you know, side by side.
sentences.zh: 美国和以色列坚如磐石地站在同一阵线，而不仅仅是并肩作战。

sentences.en: Why should we treat the
sentences.zh: 我们凭什么把

sentences.en: United States as a fair-minded mediator to any talks?
sentences.zh: 美国当作任何谈判中公正无私的调解人？

sentences.en: They've responded by walking away from the table and slamming the door and, you know, are looking for somebody else to step in.
sentences.zh: 他们的回应是拂袖而去，砰地关上大门，并且，你知道的，正在寻找其他人来介入。

sentences.en: In December of last year, President Trump announced to the world that the United States would finally recognize the truth, that Jerusalem is the capital of Israel.
sentences.zh: 去年12月，特朗普总统向世界宣布，美国将最终承认一个事实，即耶路撒冷是以色列的首都。

sentences.en: We went from Ambassador Freeman to Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner.
sentences.zh: 我们从弗里德曼大使过渡到了伊万卡·特朗普和贾里德·库什纳。

sentences.en: By moving our embassy to Jerusalem, we have shown the world once again that the United States can be trusted.
sentences.zh: 通过将我们的大使馆搬到耶路撒冷，我们再次向世界表明，美国是值得信赖的。

sentences.en: We stand with our friends and our allies.
sentences.zh: 我们与我们的朋友和盟友站在一起。

sentences.en: And above all else, we've shown that the United
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我们表明了美利坚

sentences.en: States of America will do what's right, and so we have.
sentences.zh: 合众国将做正确的事情，而我们也确实这样做了。

sentences.en: Who's with Ambassador Freeman has been really quarterbacking the Trump administration's attempt at a peace process.
sentences.zh: 与弗里德曼大使一同出席的人，实际上一直在主导特朗普政府对和平进程的尝试。

sentences.en: I am here today as a proud American and the grandson of Holocaust survivors.
sentences.zh: 我今天作为一名自豪的美国人和大屠杀幸存者的孙子来到这里。

sentences.en: He hearkened back to his grandparents who had survived the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 他回顾了在浩劫中幸存下来的祖父母。

sentences.en: After the war, they built a new life in America, a beacon of hope, a land of limitless opportunity.
sentences.zh: 战后，他们在美国开启了新生活，这里是希望的灯塔，是机会无限的土地。

sentences.en: In my office in the White House, I keep a photo of them on my desk to remind me of how high the
sentences.zh: 在白宫的办公室里，我的桌上摆着一张他们的照片，提醒着我，当国家无法分清正邪、

sentences.en: stakes are when nations fail to recognize right from wrong and the decisive power America has to tip the scales in favor of the righteous.
sentences.zh: 而美国又拥有决定性力量来促使天平倾向正义一方时，赌注有多么重大。

sentences.en: It was an interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的观点。

sentences.en: In effect, I found myself wondering, as I listened to this, whether he was suggesting that, you know, like his grandparents
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我听着这些时，我不禁在想，他是否在暗示，就像他的祖父母

sentences.en: who put the Holocaust behind them, the Palestinians ought to really just put the past behind them and move on.
sentences.zh: 将大屠杀抛在脑后一样，巴勒斯坦人也真的应该把过去抛在脑后，继续前行。

sentences.en: It is now my great honor to call upon the Prime Minister of the State of Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu.
sentences.zh: 现在，我很荣幸地请出以色列国总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡。

sentences.en: You know, in Prime Minister Netanyahu's remarks, there was an energy to them that I hadn't seen before.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在内塔尼亚胡总理的讲话中，有一种我以前从未见过的活力。

sentences.en: What a glorious day.
sentences.zh: 多么光辉的一天。

sentences.en: Remember this moment.
sentences.zh: 记住这一刻。

sentences.en: There was almost palpable relief.
sentences.zh: 几乎有一种显而易见的如释重负。

sentences.en: There was genuine excitement.
sentences.zh: 有一种发自内心的兴奋。

sentences.en: This is history.
sentences.zh: 这就是历史。

sentences.en: He talked historically, but he also talked very personally.
sentences.zh: 他的谈吐既具有历史感，又非常具有个人色彩。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you that I spent the first three years of my life in this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你们，我生命中的前三年就是在这个街区度过的。

sentences.en: He had lived just a few blocks from the embassy site and recalled walking through what then were fields with his older brother and being warned, you know, don't go too far.
sentences.zh: 他曾住在距离大使馆选址仅几个街区的地方，回忆起自己曾和哥哥走过当时还是田野的地方，并得到警告，你知道的，不要走太远。

sentences.en: Don't go up where the embassy actually sits now.
sentences.zh: 不要走到现在大使馆实际所在的地方。

sentences.en: Because my mother told me, you can't go any further.
sentences.zh: 因为我母亲告诉我，你不能再往前走了。

sentences.en: This was near the border.
sentences.zh: 这里靠近边境。

sentences.en: It was exposed to sniper fire.
sentences.zh: 它暴露在狙击手的射程之内。

sentences.en: Because that would put the two of them in sniper range from the Jordanian side.
sentences.zh: 因为这会让他们两人处于约旦方面狙击手的射程内。

sentences.en: That was then.
sentences.zh: 那是过去。

sentences.en: This is now.
sentences.zh: 这是现在。

sentences.en: Today, today, the embassy of the most powerful nation on earth.
sentences.zh: 今天，就在今天，世界上最强大国家的大使馆。

sentences.en: Our greatest ally, the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 我们最伟大的盟友，美利坚合众国。

sentences.en: Today, its embassy opened here.
sentences.zh: 今天，它的大使馆在这里揭幕。

sentences.en: Netanyahu was born in 1949.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡出生于1949年。

sentences.en: You know, he's just a year younger than the country itself.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他只比这个国家本身小一岁。

sentences.en: So he's really, he could chart his own life by its life cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以他真的可以通过这个国家的生命周期来规划自己的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: Last December, President Trump became the first world leader to recognize Jerusalem as our capital.
sentences.zh: 去年12月，特朗普总统成为第一位承认耶路撒冷为我们首都的世界领导人。

sentences.en: And today, the United States of America is opening its embassy right here in Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 而今天，美利坚合众国正在耶路撒冷这里开设大使馆。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, President Trump, for having the courage to keep your promises.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，特朗普总统，感谢你有勇气兑现承诺。

sentences.en: David, is all this happening because Donald Trump is in office?
sentences.zh: 大卫，这一切发生是因为唐纳德·特朗普在任吗？

sentences.en: In other words, does this reflect a larger shift in the way that Americans are thinking about Israel?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是否反映了美国人对以色列看法的一个更大转变？

sentences.en: Or is it all about his administration and its vantage point on this?
sentences.zh: 还是说这完全取决于他的政府及其对此事的立场？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, what are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在谈论什么？

sentences.en: Are we talking just about the embassy move?
sentences.zh: 我们仅仅是在谈论大使馆搬迁吗？

sentences.en: Are we talking about recognition of Jerusalem as the capital?
sentences.zh: 我们是在谈论承认耶路撒冷为首都吗？

sentences.en: If we're talking about those things, I don't think they happen under a different president.
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论的是这些，我认为在换一个总统的情况下它们是不会发生的。

sentences.en: I really don't.
sentences.zh: 我真的这么认为。

sentences.en: But I think you're touching on another question, which has a little bit more to do with Prime Minister Netanyahu.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你触及了另一个问题，这与内塔尼亚胡总理有更多关系。

sentences.en: The Jewish population in the United States is still heavily to the left of center.
sentences.zh: 美国的犹太人口仍然很大程度上偏向中左翼。

sentences.en: Many of the things and the policies that Mr. Netanyahu's right-wing government has been pursuing in Israel have alienated American Jews, aggravated them,
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡先生的右翼政府在以色列推行的许多事情和政策，疏远了美国犹太人，激怒了他们，

sentences.en: made them question their support for Israel, or made it difficult to defend their support for
sentences.zh: 让他们质疑自己对以色列的支持，或者在许多方面难以辩护他们对

sentences.en: Israel in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 以色列的支持。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Netanyahu has been cleaving so tightly to President
sentences.zh: 与此同时，内塔尼亚胡与特朗普

sentences.en: Trump that for Democrats in the United States, it's increasingly hard to take.
sentences.zh: 总统贴得如此之近，以至于对于美国的民主党人来说，这越来越难以忍受。

sentences.en: And David, what about average Israelis?
sentences.zh: 大卫，普通以色列人呢？

sentences.en: How did they feel about the relocation of the embassy from
sentences.zh: 他们如何看待大使馆从

sentences.en: Tel Aviv to Jerusalem?
sentences.zh: 特拉维夫搬迁至耶路撒冷？

sentences.en: This is a very divided country politically.
sentences.zh: 这是一个政治上高度分裂的国家。

sentences.en: But the move of the embassy, I was pretty surprised to learn that even left-leaning Israelis and politicians really could get behind it.
sentences.zh: 但对于大使馆的搬迁，我很惊讶地发现，甚至连偏左翼的以色列人和政客也真的能够支持它。

sentences.en: For many people, the fact that Israel alone really in the world had this very recognizable, very well-established
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，世界上唯独以色列拥有这个广为人知、根基深厚的

sentences.en: capital city that was denied the recognition that they believed it deserved was galling and grating.
sentences.zh: 首都城市，却被剥夺了他们认为应得的承认，这让人感到恼火和刺耳。

sentences.en: And to have that lifted, finally, is a really welcome thing.
sentences.zh: 而这种阴霾最终被驱散，实在是一件大快人心的事。

sentences.en: There's broad agreement among Israelis that Jerusalem should be seen as their capital and treated as such by the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 以色列人在这一点上有着广泛共识，即耶路撒冷应该被视为他们的首都，并受到世界其他地方的如此对待。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, and finally, David, was there any acknowledgement of these deadly protests at the ceremony today in Jerusalem, which is just, I guess, a few dozen miles away?
sentences.zh: 最后，大卫，今天在耶路撒冷举行的仪式上，有没有人承认这些致命的抗议活动？我想那里距离事发地点只有几十英里远吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jared Kushner actually did make some note of it, just very glancingly.
sentences.zh: 贾里德·库什纳确实顺带提及了一点，非常草率地带过。

sentences.en: But other than that, people there were applauding the president.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，那里的人们都在为总统欢呼。

sentences.en: They were listening to the lyrics of
sentences.zh: 他们听着《哈利路亚》

sentences.en: Hallelujah.
sentences.zh: 的歌词。

sentences.en: But it was a very striking contrast to what was happening just an hour's drive away.
sentences.zh: 但这与仅仅一个小时车程外发生的事情形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Thank you, David.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，大卫。

sentences.en: Really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Great talking to you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你交谈，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Declan, we just spoke to our colleague, David Helfinger, in Jerusalem after the dedication of the new
sentences.zh: 好的，德克兰，我们刚刚同我们在耶路撒冷的同事大卫·赫尔芬格进行了交谈，就在新

sentences.en: American embassy there.
sentences.zh: 美国驻耶路撒冷大使馆举行落成典礼之后。

sentences.en: What's going on in Gaza as that is happening?
sentences.zh: 在那期间，加沙发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, it's been, to put it simply, it's been the bloodiest day in Gaza since 2014.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，简单来说，这是自2014年以来加沙最血腥的一天。

sentences.en: Declan Walsh covers the Middle East for The Times.
sentences.zh: 德克兰·沃尔什为《泰晤士报》报道中东新闻。

sentences.en: Today, we had 55 protesters killed on the Palestinian side of the fence that separates Gaza from Israel.
sentences.zh: 今天，在隔离加沙与以色列的铁丝网巴勒斯坦一侧，有55名抗议者丧生。

sentences.en: And we had approximately 2,400 people who were wounded in those clashes.
sentences.zh: 在这些冲突中，大约有2400人受伤。

sentences.en: Either by rifle fire from Israeli soldiers positioned on the other side of the fence, or from lesser injuries due to gear gas.
sentences.zh: 有的是被部署在铁丝网另一侧的以色列士兵的步枪火力击伤，有的则是由于催泪瓦斯造成的较轻伤势。

sentences.en: To be honest, I can mostly describe it as it looks something like a medieval battleground today, where, you know, you have a long fence running down the middle.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我大体上可以把它形容得像今天的某处中世纪战场，你知道，中间有一道长长的铁丝网延伸开来。

sentences.en: You have a long berm on the Israeli side that has military posts with soldiers inside them, dotted along the fence.
sentences.zh: 以色列一侧有一道长长的土堤，上面建有军事哨所，士兵们驻守在里面，沿着铁丝网星罗棋布。

sentences.en: And on the Palestinian side, where the protesters have been burning tires, so the air has been filled with this sort of inky black smoke.
sentences.zh: 在巴勒斯坦一侧，抗议者一直在焚烧轮胎，因此空气中弥漫着这种浓黑的墨烟。

sentences.en: You have these kite bombs.
sentences.zh: 你们有这种风筝炸弹。

sentences.en: Kite bombs?
sentences.zh: 风筝炸弹？

sentences.en: That's right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: The protesters, they make these kites that they paint Palestinian flags or emblems on.
sentences.zh: 抗议者制作了这些风筝，并在上面绘制了巴勒斯坦国旗或徽章。

sentences.en: And then they attach sort of crude explosive devices.
sentences.zh: 然后他们附上某种简易爆炸装置。

sentences.en: In many cases, it might be, say, a bag of sugar that is soaked in gasoline.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，它可能是一袋浸透了汽油的糖之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then it is attached to a flame device.
sentences.zh: 然后将其连接到一个火焰装置上。

sentences.en: They set the kite into the air.
sentences.zh: 他们将风筝放飞到空中。

sentences.en: And then as it is burning, it has this sort of flaming tail.
sentences.zh: 当它燃烧时，它会拖着一条类似火焰的尾巴。

sentences.en: They guide it towards the Israeli border.
sentences.zh: 他们引导它飞向以色列边境。

sentences.en: And they try to land it in fields on the other side to set the Israeli crops on fire.
sentences.zh: 他们试图让它落在另一侧的田野里，以便点燃以色列的农作物。

sentences.en: You have Israeli drones that are monitoring, or in some instances, it appears, firing tear gas as well over the area.
sentences.zh: 你们有以色列的无人机在监控，或者在某些情况下，似乎也在该地区上空发射催泪瓦斯。

sentences.en: And then you have ambulances that are screaming, rushing to pick up people who've been shot or wounded.
sentences.zh: 然后是救护车发出尖叫声，争分夺秒地赶去接运那些被枪击或受伤的人。

sentences.en: And then when you push further back, away from the front line of it, you have a whole sort of staging area where families are hanging out,
sentences.zh: 当你把视线进一步推远，离开最前线时，你会看到一整片集结区，家属们在那里闲逛，

sentences.en: where people are speaking into microphones, trying to urge people forward, where there is music and food.
sentences.zh: 人们对着话筒讲话，试图敦促大家向前推进，那里有音乐和食物。

sentences.en: Leaders from the main militant factions in Gaza addressed thousands of worshippers.
sentences.zh: 加沙主要武装派别的领导人向数千名信徒发表了讲话。

sentences.en: They launched a lot of rhetorical attacks against the United States, which they described as the great Satan.
sentences.zh: 他们对美国发起了大量的言论攻击，将其描述为“大撒旦”。

sentences.en: They attacked Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们抨击了特朗普。

sentences.en: And they spoke about this decision to move the embassy to Jerusalem as a great betrayal.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到将大使馆迁往耶路撒冷的决定是一场巨大的背叛。

sentences.en: Because, of course, for Muslims, and particularly for the Palestinians, they consider Jerusalem to be a sacred city.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，对于穆斯林，尤其是对于巴勒斯坦人来说，他们认为耶路撒冷是一座圣城。

sentences.en: And they consider eastern Jerusalem to be a place where they could potentially have the capital of a future Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 他们认为东耶路撒冷是一个他们未来可能建立巴勒斯坦国首都的地方。

sentences.en: For many Palestinians, the declaration by the Trump administration that it was going to move the embassy to Jerusalem
sentences.zh: 对于许多巴勒斯坦人来说，特朗普政府宣布将把大使馆迁往耶路撒冷，

sentences.en: really signaled that the Americans are no longer willing to play the role of being an impartial mediator between them and the Israelis in their historical struggle.
sentences.zh: 这实际上表明，美国人不再愿意在他们与以色列人的历史斗争中扮演公正调解人的角色。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the rhetoric that I heard on the ground today for these protests was specifically directed at the United States.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我在抗议现场听到的大量言论都是针对美国的。

sentences.en: Gaza is this area that he's been under an Israeli blockade for the last 11 years.
sentences.zh: 加沙这个地区在过去11年里一直处于以色列的封锁之下。

sentences.en: The territory is controlled by the militant group Hamas, which is backed by Iran.
sentences.zh: 该领土由得到伊朗支持的武装组织哈马斯控制。

sentences.en: Hamas has fought several wars with Israel that have been very destructive, that have reduced rubble, large parts of Gaza.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯与以色列进行了数次极具破坏性的战争，将加沙的大片地区化为废墟。

sentences.en: And some of that is now rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分现在已经重建。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, this remains a very impoverished place.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，这里仍然是一个非常贫困的地方。

sentences.en: It's also a place that is largely cut off from the outside world.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个基本与世隔绝的地方。

sentences.en: All supplies of food, medicine, cement, all the basics are strictly controlled by the government of Israel.
sentences.zh: 所有的粮食、药品、水泥供应以及所有基本物资都受到以色列政府的严格控制。

sentences.en: And the people who live here, for them, it's almost impossible to leave.
sentences.zh: 对于生活在这里的人们来说，离开几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: So, so many of the young people I spoke to today who are participating in the protest, they have not only never visited other countries in the region,
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我交谈过的许多参加抗议的年轻人，不仅从未访问过该地区的其他国家，

sentences.en: most of them haven't even seen Israel.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数甚至连以色列都没见过。

sentences.en: So for them, their view of an Israeli or of what Israel looks like is really limited to these soldiers that they see standing at the border posts along the fence.
sentences.zh: 因此对他们而言，他们对以色列人或以色列样貌的看法，实际上仅限于他们看到的可在沿铁丝网边境哨所站岗的这些士兵。

sentences.en: And right now, making a very concerted effort to stop them trying to breach that fence or to come across it.
sentences.zh: 而此刻，他们正做出极其坚决的努力，阻止这些人试图突破铁丝网或跨越过来。

sentences.en: So we've seen through the day, people will come towards the fence, there will be warning shots, then they tend to shoot people in the leg.
sentences.zh: 所以我们整天都看到，人们会朝铁丝网走来，会有鸣枪警告，然后他们往往会朝人们的腿部开枪。

sentences.en: But certainly anybody who has gotten as close as the fence seems to be in danger of suffering a lethal shot.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，任何靠近到铁丝网附近的人似乎都有遭受致命枪击的危险。

sentences.en: So there were a number of people we saw who were killed at the fence today, who appeared to have been shot in the head by Israeli snipers,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到今天在铁丝网处有一些人丧生，他们似乎是被以色列狙击手击中了头部，

sentences.en: who are positioned on top of berms that overlook the fence and provide them a view over what's going on.
sentences.zh: 狙击手部署在俯瞰铁丝网的土堤顶上，这为他们提供了俯瞰事态发展的视野。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Are you surprised by that use of force?
sentences.zh: 你对这种武力的使用感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Gunshots, especially to the head of people walking up to the fence?
sentences.zh: 枪击，尤其是对走向铁丝网的人的头部开枪？

sentences.en: I mean, the Israelis say that this is what is necessary to prevent people coming through and to protect the sovereignty of their country
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，以色列人说，这是阻止人们闯入、保护他们国家主权所必要的，

sentences.en: and also to protect the Israeli communities that are living on the other side of this fence.
sentences.zh: 同时也是为了保护生活在这个铁丝网另一侧的以色列社区。

sentences.en: But, you know, any Palestinian that you speak to will tell you, and certainly some international organizations also will complain that this is a disproportionate use of force.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你与之交谈的任何巴勒斯坦人都会告诉你，当然一些国际组织也会抱怨，这是过度的武力使用。

sentences.en: When you speak to people who are trying to go across the fence and you say, you know, what would you do if you actually get to the other side?
sentences.zh: 当你同那些试图穿过铁丝网的人交谈并问他们，你知道的，如果你真的到了另一侧你会怎么做？

sentences.en: It's hard to get a strong answer.
sentences.zh: 很难得到一个强有力的回答。

sentences.en: And you get the impression that for many people, the goal is to breach the fence and to make this kind of symbolic gesture rather than to get through on the other side.
sentences.zh: 给人的印象是，对许多人来说，目标是突破铁丝网并做出这种象征性的姿态，而不是真正穿到另一侧。

sentences.en: Because I think most people realize that there is such a heavy military presence all the way along the fence that even if they were to breach it,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为大多数人意识到，沿铁丝网一路都有如此强大的军事存在，即使他们真的突破了，

sentences.en: I mean, at the very best, they would possibly be arrested and at worst, they would be shot dead.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，往最好里说，他们可能会被捕，往最坏里说，他们会被枪杀。

sentences.en: But this may be an opportunity for them to win international sympathy, to play in the court of public opinion.
sentences.zh: 但这可能是他们赢得国际同情、在舆论法庭上发挥作用的一个机会。

sentences.en: But of course, at a terrible, terrible cost, as we saw with so many people shot and wounded today.
sentences.zh: 但当然，代价是极其惨重的，正如我们今天看到那么多人中枪受伤一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Even if they were to breach the fence, you're saying it doesn't seem like it would really matter, they'd be outmatched, outgunned,
sentences.zh: 即使他们真的突破了铁丝网，你的意思是这似乎也无关紧要，他们寡不敌众，火力悬殊，

sentences.en: that this is really about the symbolism of drawing attention to their cause.
sentences.zh: 这实际上关乎通过引起人们对其事业的关注来体现象征意义。

sentences.en: And perhaps that's really the goal.
sentences.zh: 也许这才是真正的目标。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样的。

sentences.en: Has anyone breached the fence?
sentences.zh: 有人突破铁丝网了吗？

sentences.en: The fence, in reality, is actually several layers in many places.
sentences.zh: 现实中的铁丝网在许多地方实际上是由好几层组成的。

sentences.en: So there will be an electronic fence, then there may be a ditch, then there could be a high berm on the other side.
sentences.zh: 所以会有一道电子栅栏，然后可能有一条沟渠，然后另一侧可能有一道高高的土堤。

sentences.en: But so there have been instances where protesters have pulled back the wire and maybe gotten through the first layer,
sentences.zh: 不过也有抗议者拉开铁丝并可能穿过第一层的情况，

sentences.en: but certainly nobody seems to have gone through the multiple layers and come out the other side in Israel proper.
sentences.zh: 但显然没有人真正穿过多层铁丝网并从以色列本土的另一侧出来。

sentences.en: Some of the protesters I spoke to today, they described how they had spent their afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我今天交谈的一些抗议者描述了他们是如何度过下午的。

sentences.en: They had gone to the front of the proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们来到了抗议活动的最前线。

sentences.en: They had run the risk of being shot by snipers.
sentences.zh: 他们冒着被狙击手枪击的风险。

sentences.en: If they managed to push forward to the fence itself, they were engulfed in these clouds of either tire smoke that their own side had created, or they were engulfed in tear gas
sentences.zh: 如果他们设法向前推进到铁丝网本身，他们就会被自己这一方制造的轮胎烟雾云所吞没，或者被催泪瓦斯所吞没，

sentences.en: that the Israelis were firing from the far side.
sentences.zh: 那是以色列人从远端发射的。

sentences.en: And then one young man I was speaking to told me about how one person beside him was shot in the leg, another person coming up behind him was shot in the head.
sentences.zh: 然后，我正在交谈的一位年轻人告诉我，他身旁的一个人腿部中枪，另一个紧随其后过来的人头部中枪。

sentences.en: He managed to avoid all of that.
sentences.zh: 他设法避开了所有这些。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, I said, what did you achieve?
sentences.zh: 但在一天结束时，我问，你们取得了什么成就？

sentences.en: And he said, well, I managed to pull back a number of pieces of wire and then I got through the first layer and I hid behind a little concrete wall for a while and then I ran back.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我设法拉回了几段铁丝，然后我穿过了第一层，在一堵小混凝土墙后面躲了一会儿，然后我又跑了回来。

sentences.en: And he said, for him, that was success for today.
sentences.zh: 他说，对她而言，那是今天的成功。

sentences.en: That was an achievement.
sentences.zh: 那是一个成就。

sentences.en: At the best, the goal is to cut some wire and pull back a couple of bales of wire.
sentences.zh: 往最好里说，目标就是割断一些铁丝并拉回几捆铁丝。

sentences.en: And those are the trophies, if you like, that you see young people carrying back from the fence these lumps of wire that they've managed to take out of it,
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，那些就是你看到年轻人从铁丝网上带回来的战利品——他们设法从中弄出来的几团铁丝，

sentences.en: but not really to put a serious breach in the fence itself.
sentences.zh: 但并没有真正在铁丝网本身上撕开一个重大的缺口。

sentences.en: I have to say, that seems extremely futile and kind of sad that people who are demanding something so big are going away with something so small.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这看起来极其徒劳，也有些可悲，那些要求如此宏大目标的人最后却只带着这么微不足道的东西离开。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you've got to ask yourself why, if you were a young Gazan, you would want to take these huge risks to your life to push towards this fence,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，你不得不问自己，如果你是一个加沙的年轻人，你为什么要冒着生命危险向这个铁丝网推进，

sentences.en: knowing that you could be shot down by an Israeli soldier on the other side.
sentences.zh: 明知自己可能会被另一侧的以色列士兵击倒。

sentences.en: And when you talk to people and you get beyond the kind of the rhetoric and the politics, what you really get to often is just this sense of desperation.
sentences.zh: 当你与人们交谈，抛开那些言辞和政治时，你真正接触到的往往只是这种绝望感。

sentences.en: You know, young people who will say, you know, I've never left this territory.
sentences.zh: 你知道，年轻人会说，你知道的，我从未离开过这片领土。

sentences.en: I have no job.
sentences.zh: 我没有工作。

sentences.en: I'm living with my parents, but I'm unable to get married because I have no money.
sentences.zh: 我和父母住在一起，但我结不了婚，因为我没有钱。

sentences.en: And so there's a sort of attitude of people saying, well, to be honest, I don't have much to lose.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们有一种态度，那就是，老实说，我没什么可失去的。

sentences.en: So for me, these kind of protests are an opportunity to express myself.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这类抗议活动是一个表达自我的机会。

sentences.en: And even if that involves a threat to my life or the potential of being killed, that's the threat that I'm willing to take in order to make this point
sentences.zh: 即使这涉及对我的生命的威胁或被杀害的可能，为了表明这一观点，

sentences.en: and to try and project their point of view into the world.
sentences.zh: 并试图将他们的观点投射到世界上，这也是我愿意承担的威胁。

sentences.en: Finally, our colleague David was saying that when the Israeli state was recognized 70 years ago, this joyous moment for Israelis, that same day is remembered
sentences.zh: 最后，我们的同事大卫一直在说，当以色列国在70年前被承认时，对于以色列人来说这是一个欢乐的时刻，但同一天却被巴勒斯坦人铭记

sentences.en: as the catastrophe for Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 为灾难日。

sentences.en: And it feels like here we are again,
sentences.zh: 感觉我们又回到了这里，

sentences.en: 70 years later to the day, with these two groups experiencing the same thing, the declaration of the embassy, as in one case, a moment of great joy,
sentences.zh: 整整70年后的今天，这两个群体经历着同样的事情，大使馆的宣布在一种情况下是一个充满巨大欢乐的时刻，

sentences.en: and in the other, as the ultimate injustice.
sentences.zh: 而在另一种情况下，则是终极的不公。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You just have to look at the contrasting scenes on this very small patch of land.
sentences.zh: 你只需看看这片极小的土地上截然不同的场景。

sentences.en: You know, today you had in Jerusalem, the ceremony at the embassy, and then 60 miles down the road inside Gaza, you had these scenes of despair, of violence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，今天你在耶路撒冷看到了大使馆的典礼，然后沿着公路走60英里在加沙内部，你看到了绝望、暴力的场景。

sentences.en: And really, I think for Palestinians, even the things that they thought that they could count on, for instance, the fact that the US would at least consider holding out
sentences.zh: 真的，我认为对于巴勒斯坦人来说，甚至连他们认为自己可以依靠的事情——例如，美国至少会考虑将

sentences.en: the position of the embassy as a bargaining chip and potential negotiations with the Israelis, that has been snatched away from them as well.
sentences.zh: 大使馆的立场作为与以色列人进行潜在谈判的筹码这一事实——也被从他们手中残忍夺走了。

sentences.en: And the decision to move the embassy is really seen as an emblem of what they call that treachery.
sentences.zh: 而搬迁大使馆的决定真的被视为他们所称的那种背叛的象征。

sentences.en: Declan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 德克兰，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: It was a pleasure to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴与你交谈。

sentences.en: Thank you, too.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你。

sentences.en: In Washington, a spokesman for President Trump,
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，特朗普总统的发言人

sentences.en: Raj Shah, blamed the casualties on Palestinian leaders in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 拉杰·沙阿将加沙的伤亡归咎于加沙的巴勒斯坦领导人。

sentences.en: Well, we're aware of the reports of continued violence in Gaza today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们知道今天加沙持续发生暴力的报道。

sentences.en: The responsibility for these tragic deaths rests squarely with Hamas.
sentences.zh: 这些悲惨死亡的责任完全在哈马斯。

sentences.en: Hamas is intentionally and cynically provoking this response.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯是在蓄意且玩世不恭地煽动这种反应。

sentences.en: And as the Secretary of State said,
sentences.zh: 正如国务卿所说，

sentences.en: Israel has the right to defend itself.
sentences.zh: 以色列有权保卫自己。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: On Monday, the Supreme Court struck down a federal law that had effectively banned commercial sports betting in most states for the past 25 years.
sentences.zh: 周一，最高法院推翻了一项联邦法律，该法律在过去25年中实际上禁止了大多数州的商业体育博彩。

sentences.en: The case revolved around a 1992 law that prohibited states from authorizing sports gambling over fears that it could lead to cheating by athletes and coaches.
sentences.zh: 此案围绕1992年的一项法律展开，该法律禁止各州授权体育博彩，因为担心这会导致运动员和教练作弊。

sentences.en: But a majority of the justices ruled that the law violated states' rights under the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 但多数大法官裁定，该法律违反了宪法赋予各州的权利。

sentences.en: The Times reports that as a result of the ruling, sports betting is expected to quickly expand across the country.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，由于这一裁决，体育博彩预计将在全国范围内迅速扩大。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》节目到此结束。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称是改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
